question: If sec theta + tan theta = 4 + sqrt{15}, { then find the value of } sec theta - tan theta.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use identity: (secθ + tanθ)(secθ − tanθ) = 1

⇒ secθ − tanθ = 1 / (4 + √15)

Rationalize ⇒ = (4 − √15) / (16 − 15)

= 4 − √15

**∴ Answer = 4 − √15**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

secθ + tanθ = 4 + √15

**Formula used:**

(secθ + tanθ)(secθ − tanθ) = sec²θ − tan²θ = 1

**Calculation:**

⇒ (secθ + tanθ)(secθ − tanθ) = 1

⇒ (4 + √15)(secθ − tanθ) = 1

⇒ secθ − tanθ = 1 / (4 + √15)

⇒ Multiply numerator & denominator by (4 − √15)

⇒ = (4 − √15) / (16 − 15)

⇒ = 4 − √15

**∴ The correct answer is 4 − √15.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Key Identity

sec²θ − tan²θ = 1

Important Relation

(secθ + tanθ)(secθ − tanθ) = 1

Rationalization

Multiply by conjugate to simplify surds

Quick Tip

If one expression is given, the other is its reciprocal
